audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers ran Skill, Vladimir, Vladimir, Skill, Skill, Vladimir, Vladimir while the whys described the opposite shape: Vladimir owning level 1, the level-3 rotation being yours when Pool is down, levels 4-5 being your low point, and 6 / first item being your windows.
audit.why: Vladimir's level 1 is free — Transfusion costs no mana and heals. Your low point is 4-5 pre-Tear. Your windows are 6 (Warp) and Seraph's. The packet chart matches that and the 48.14% win rate matches a lane you lose late.
audit.corrected: Vladimir, Skill, Skill, Vladimir, Ryze, Ryze, Vladimir — paired full/content rows with ratings moved to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sanguine Pool's cooldown was written as 26 seconds in whys[2] and in the early block, and one Do's entry called it a 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: Riot's data gives 28/25/22/19/16. At rank 1 it is 28 seconds — the single most schedule-relevant number in the matchup, and it was wrong in two places and absent in a third.
audit.corrected: All three corrected to 28 seconds at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never stated that Tides of Blood is blocked by enemy units, and never stated Ryze's own ordering constraint (W only roots through Flux).
audit.why: Riot's text for Vladimir's E: the released blood 'can be blocked by enemy units' — so standing behind your wave removes his main poke. Ryze's W roots only if Flux is already on the target; against a champion whose answer is a 2-second untargetable pool, the E-first ordering is what makes the root land at all.
audit.corrected: Minion-block written into the Do's; Flux-before-W ordering written into the level-2 phase.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal was mentioned only in the itemization line, with no timing.
audit.why: Transfusion heals on a 9s-to-4.6s cooldown and Hemoplague heals per champion hit — Grievous Wounds timing decides every extended trade.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds moved into the Don'ts as a precondition for extending, and into the levels 4-5 phase where his sustain is winning.

edits.before: Q poke only — farm, respect everything, and bank Manaflow stacks. You're buying time, not fighting.
edits.after: Transfusion costs him nothing and heals at 600 — farm from Q's 1000 and bank Manaflow stacks.

edits.before: W root threatens jungle follow-up, but it's also your kite tool — spending it greedily is how you die.
edits.after: Sanguine Pool eats a raw W for 28s at rank 1 — land E first or the root is only a wasted slow.

edits.before: Phase Rush turns his engage into your trade window — combo, proc the speed, and walk away untouched.
edits.after: Your mana costs peak pre-Tear while Tides of Blood costs him health only — farm and buy Grievous Wounds.

edits.before: Seraph's online — you out-DPS and out-tank everyone in extended fights. Side-lane and Warp to every fight.
edits.after: Rylai's plus Pool means one W root never pins him — Warp your team into fights instead of dueling.

edits.before: Full E-Q-W rotation is live and Sanguine Pool has a 26-second cooldown — if you E-Flux him first and his Pool is down, W into empowered Q lands the full Flux cascade.
edits.after: Full E-Q-W rotation is live and Sanguine Pool has a 28-second cooldown — if you E-Flux him first and his Pool is down, W into empowered Q lands the full Flux cascade.

edits.before: At level 1 Vladimir's Q outranges your walk-up and gives him free HP while you take poke trying to CS. You have no root yet so he can Q-trade and step back freely — do not fight, stack Manaflow Band charges and accept the chip damage. At level 2 your W comes online and you have a real threat: W-root into empowered Q deals more burst than his Q sustain can recover if you land it, but the risk is that he simply activates Sanguine Pool to dodge the root and reset the whole exchange in his favor. Level 3 is your first real window — E onto him to apply Flux, immediately W-root (Sanguine Pool has a 26-second cooldown at rank 1 and he won't always have it), then empowered Q into Flux-marked target for the bounce cascade. If he pools your W, stop the combo immediately and disengage: your empowered Q will whiff and you've spent your mana for nothing.
edits.after: At level 1 Vladimir's Q outranges your walk-up and gives him free HP while you take poke trying to CS. Level 3 is your first real window — E onto him to apply Flux, immediately W-root (Sanguine Pool has a 28-second cooldown at rank 1 and he won't always have it), then empowered Q into Flux-marked target for the bounce cascade. If he pools your W, stop the combo immediately and disengage: your empowered Q will whiff and you've spent your mana for nothing.

edits.before: Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Tides of Blood is blocked by minions — keep the wave between you, and bait Pool before you spend a combo.

edits.before: Vladimir burns Sanguine Pool on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Vladimir burns Sanguine Pool on nothing — take the whole 28-second invitation.

edits.before: That’s Vladimir’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Transfusion heals off every trade — buy Grievous Wounds before you extend.

notes: Sanguine Pool is 2 seconds of untargetability, not a cleanse — a root already applied is not removed by Riot's text alone, but whether the pool clears an existing root is not stated in the kit data, so nothing was written either way. All Pool advice is framed as 'bait it before you commit', which is true regardless. Rylai's is named in inherited text as his two-item spike; left as-is, not verified from the kits.
